checks.statement: For a generator g of cyclic order n >= 2, {g,g^{-1}} has cardinality 2 exactly when n != 2.
checks.reasoning: g=g^{-1} is equivalent to g^2=1. Since the order of g is n, this means n divides 2; together with n>=2 it gives n=2. Thus the inverse pair has two distinct elements precisely for n!=2.
checks.outcome: Consistent with the written condition in the added parenthesis. This does not decide its shorthand sss/ssi/ss, nor any uncertain glyph elsewhere.

checks.statement: The proposed two-element Omega formulation retains two elements when n=2.
checks.reasoning: For a cyclic group of order 2, its generator is its own inverse. Sending both a and b of a two-element Omega to this generator satisfies i(a)i(b)=1, while the image pair in G has only one element.
checks.outcome: The replacement formulation addresses the order-2 collapse described around the bullets. This is a local consistency check, not a proof of the full contour classification.
